clue.text: Socks, maybe churchwarden's gardening gear

parts.note: socks are an example of hose, the old word for legwear
a churchwarden is a long-stemmed clay pipe

explanation.surface: A churchwarden's socks are listed, oddly, among his kit for tending the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Churchwarden' looks like a parish officer, but it is the long clay pipe named after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosepipe is the flexible tube used for watering plants, a standard piece of garden equipment.

clue.text: Rolling Stone who bought sandwiches

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer between its letters as bread holds a filling

explanation.surface: A member of the Rolling Stones went out for sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling Stone' suggests the band, but it means one who rolls, a wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobo is a wandering vagrant, like the proverbial rolling stone that gathers no moss.

clue.text: Noon service? It's on time

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A midday church service is running on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sext is the canonical office said at the sixth hour, around midday, in monastic prayer.

clue.text: Rang a licentiate in profound reflection

indicators.note: in places the pair inside the mirrored word
a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: deep means profound
L is an abbreviation for licentiate

explanation.surface: A licensed professional phoned while deep in thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflection' turns DEEP into PEED; A and L go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bells pealed when they rang out loudly together.

clue.text: Men put energy into old contest for real money

parts.note: chessmen are also called pieces

indicators.note: put marks placing one piece somewhere in another
into says the energy goes inside the contest word

parts.note: a fight is a contest
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Fighters inject vigour into an ancient bout staged for genuine cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'real' is not 'genuine' but the old Spanish coin; a piece of eight was worth eight reals.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of eight were Spanish dollars valued at eight reales, literally money counted in reals.

clue.text: Forced to work one's way up in Palladium

indicators.note: in places the climbing word inside the chemical symbol

parts.note: Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium
to rise is to work one's way up in a career

explanation.surface: A performer forced to climb the ladder at the London Palladium theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Palladium is a famous West End theatre, but here it is the chemical element, symbol PD.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something is to force it open or out with leverage, so prised means forced.

clue.text: Some players at Twickers rifle kitbag

parts.note: a ruck is a loose group of rugby players over the ball; Twickers is slang for Twickenham, England's rugby stadium
to rifle a place is to ransack or sack it

explanation.surface: Rugby players at Twickenham go through a sports bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun but is the verb meaning to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack is a bag carried on the back, used for carrying kit.

clue.text: Every rep needs such protection, should limb be broken

definitions.meaning: a repertory theatre company needs actors in minor roles
a plaster ... supports and protects a broken arm or leg

explanation.surface: Every sales rep should carry insurance in case of a broken limb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rep' suggests a salesperson or gym repetition, but it is a repertory theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: secondary actors in a play, and a plaster cast that holds a fractured bone.

clue.text: Crush food prepared and consumed with right filling

parts.note: a dish is food prepared for the table

indicators.note: the right letter fills the middle of the eating word

parts.note: eaten means consumed

explanation.surface: A recipe: food is made and eaten with something good inside, then crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishearten is to dispirit, and to crush someone is to dash their hopes.

clue.text: One takes pictures rolled up by artist on set

indicators.note: in an across answer the rolled-up piece on the set piece is written after it

parts.note: the box is slang for a television set
to roll up is to arrive, so rolled up means came
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A photographer arrives with a painter to take shots on a film set.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer 'on' puts the set first; 'by' adds the artist after. 'Rolled up' suggests film rolls but just means arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A box camera is a simple early camera, a device that takes photographs.

clue.text: A land with military commander elected time after time

parts.note: to land something is to gain or win it
and means together with
an aga is an Ottoman military commander
in means elected, as a party voted in

explanation.surface: A country gets an army chief voted into power, over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Again and again means repeatedly, the same idea as time after time.

clue.text: Leader pushed to back of room gets through

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for room is shifted to its tail end

parts.note: scope means room, as in room for manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A boss relegated to the back of the room still manages to get by.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage or get by, so copes means gets through a difficulty.

clue.text: Officers rent retail outlet

parts.note: generals are senior army officers
rent as a past tense means tore

explanation.surface: Army officers lease a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' reads as a payment or leasing, but it is the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: A general store is a shop selling a wide variety of goods, a kind of retail business.

clue.text: US sportsman ultimately losing in row with some clubs

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the row word

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the next word

parts.note: woods are a type of golf club

explanation.surface: An American athlete in the end loses an argument with some golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but is a line of seats, TIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is the American golfer, one of the most famous US sportsmen.

clue.text: Cryptically 'trad' items carried forward to the next meeting?

definitions.text: items carried forward to the next meeting?

parts.note: read cryptically, trad is the word trade, meaning commerce, with its last letter missing

explanation.surface: A cryptic note about traditional jazz items deferred to the next meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trad' suggests traditional jazz; read as wordplay, trad is TRADE (business) with its end missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfinished business is agenda items not dealt with and held over to a later meeting.

clue.text: Taverns in France avoided by north Europeans

indicators.note: the north Europeans steer clear of France, so its letter is dropped from them

parts.note: Finns are people from Finland in northern Europe
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Scandinavian travellers shun French taverns.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are pubs or taverns offering drink and often lodging.

clue.text: Rule applied to criminal faction or one cheating partner

indicators.note: a criminal arrangement of the words is a crooked one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A law aimed at a lawless gang, or at someone two-timing a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' makes FORNICATO from FACTION OR, and R for rule follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fornicator is someone who has sex outside marriage, here one being unfaithful to a partner.

clue.text: See 14
Might they demolish a nice supper, having spent a penny?

definitions.text: Might they demolish a nice supper, having spent a penny?

indicators.note: to demolish is to wreck, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: spending the coin means it is gone, so its letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Diners who wolf down a good meal, after a trip to the loo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spent a penny' is British slang for using the toilet; here it drops one P from SUPPER, and 'demolish' rearranges A NICE SUPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicureans are lovers of fine food and drink, people who would happily devour a good meal.

clue.text: As soon as possible, couple cleared out

parts.note: on means possible or feasible, as in 'that's not on'

indicators.note: emptying the word of its insides leaves only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pair are evicted at the earliest opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As soon as possible' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Once can mean as soon as or the moment that, as in 'once you arrive, call me'.

clue.text: Praise diverse kingdom of old

indicators.note: diverse means varied, so the letters take a varied order

explanation.surface: Extol an ancient realm of many peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Persia was the ancient empire and later kingdom, now known as Iran.

clue.text: Item for man of letters said to be correcting journal

indicators.note: said marks that what follows is spoken, sounding like another word

parts.note: righting means correcting
a paper is a newspaper or journal

explanation.surface: A literary figure is reported to be putting a periodical straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is stationery used by someone writing letters, the letter-writer's basic supply.

clue.text: See 7
Turn down end of alley, following retreat

indicators.note: following puts the alley letter after the retreat word

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

indicators.note: end of picks out the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Directions: turn at the end of the alley after going back.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny a request is to turn it down or refuse it.

clue.text: Taps into source of mineral pigment

indicators.note: into places the taps inside the source word

parts.note: ore is rock that is mined as a source of mineral
C and H stand for the cold and hot taps

explanation.surface: Tapping a mineral deposit to get colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment made from clay containing iron oxide.

clue.text: Put more plainly, tenor and soprano's parting was overdue

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for tenor in choral music

indicators.note: the soprano parts the phrase, splitting it apart by sitting between its pieces

parts.note: ran late means was overdue
S is an abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: A tenor and a soprano broke up, long after they should have.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to render in other words, often plainer ones, as in explaining jargon.

clue.text: Cruel perversion of son stopping legendary king's return

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the son goes inside
a return goes back, so the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Midas is the legendary king whose touch turned things to gold

explanation.surface: A son prevents the mythical king from coming back, a cruel twist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns MIDAS into SADIM, and 'stopping' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadism is taking pleasure in inflicting pain, a cruel deviation of appetite.

clue.text: Lines on baby's foot

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: an infant is a baby
RY is an abbreviation for railway, the lines

explanation.surface: Creases on the sole of an infant's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks like part of a baby, but it is the old term for soldiers on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers are infantry; 'foot' alone is the military term for the infantry.
